company_notes:
Overview: Mid-market product analytics SaaS building intelligent in-product assistant and search. Initial approach: quick hosted API pilot -> evaluate dedicated capacity for predictable latency and cost isolation.

Key business drivers: improve in-app conversion via contextual chat, 85% of queries need sub-150ms 95th pctl latency for embeddings-based search; strong cost control required (target < $0.08/token equivalent across peak hours).

Security/Compliance: requires VPC deployment option and KMS integration for customer data. SOC2 certification required; data residency preference: US only for PII-derived vectors. Legal wants audit logs and retention controls in contract.

POC summary (hosted API): 2025-12-01 demo -> 2-week hosted POC Dec 5–18: measured throughput ~350 qps for embedding batch workloads, median latency 48ms, p95 140ms (good). Cost baseline established; engineers happy with SDK ergonomics.

Decision to evaluate Dedicated: Product team flagged variable peak patterns (daily spikes up to 3x) and want guaranteed capacity with burstability. Decided to evaluate Dedicated during Jan–Feb POC to compare unit economics and tail latencies.

Dedicated POC notes: 2026-01-10 architecture workshop with SE (Omar). Ran Dedicated POC Jan 15–Feb 15: configured reserved pool (2xA100-equivalent) with KV cache. Observed 30% lower per-token cost under steady load, but required more careful autoscaling tuning for spiky weekends.

Pricing negotiations: negotiating committed throughput (GPU-hour commitments) vs burst buffer. Peakbridge prefers a 12-month commit with quarterly ramp (25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100%) to match product launch cadence. Key asks: guaranteed burst capacity of +50% sustained for short windows, clear overage pricing tiers (hourly banded discount schedule), and a cap on overage cost during first 3 months of ramp. They requested an option to swap to higher quantized model variant for cost savings and fallback routing rules documented in SLA. AE provided preliminary pricing appendix (drive link).

Legal/security review: security team requested encryption-at-rest verification for KV cache and HSM/KMS key flow diagrams. Also asked for specific audit log retention (1 year) and the right to export usage logs for internal billing reconciliation.

Commercial: CFO wants ARR-binding commitments to be adjustable on 90-day notice if product KPIs don't hit targets. Asking for break clauses and a ramp schedule tied to product milestones. Procurement looking for standard MSA with Redwood's pricing appendix and SOW.

Quote sensitivity: can expand to Dedicated if committed ARR >= $300k/yr with the requested ramp and burst terms. If commit is only $150k, they will remain on Hosted and revisit in 6 months.

Next operational items: get final committed GPU-hours and pricing tiers, security sign-off on KMS diagrams, legal to review MSA; scheduling follow-up with CFO and CTO week of 2026-03-04.
